mainTopic: שמואל's view that blood on the wrong part of the מזבח still brings כפרה, and the side discussion of an unfit person's placement and intent
overview: The משנה ruled that blood put on the wrong part of the מזבח makes the קרבן פסול. שמואל explains that only the meat is forbidden: the owners already received כפרה, because the פסוק says blood 'on the מזבח' atones, and the word 'לכפר' limits this blood to כפרה alone. The גמרא infers that שמואל holds שלא במקומו כמקומו דמי. It challenges this from a משנה that requires a fit כהן to collect fresh blood after a wrong placement. It answers that the משנה is about an unfit person who placed the blood. The גמרא then asks why the offering is not דחוי, and the discussion turns to whether an unfit person's bad intent can ruin an offering. It concludes, following רבא, that his intent counts only during שחיטה and not from קבלה onward. Finally the גמרא begins a new objection from a ברייתא about intending to put blood above or below the red line, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: שמואל: The Meat Is Disqualified, but the Owners Are Atoned
steps.stepSummary: שמואל explains that the משנה's word 'פסול' refers to the meat, while the owners still got their כפרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: שמואל says: When the משנה says 'disqualified,' it means the meat may not be eaten. But the owners have already been atoned for.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with שמואל explaining what the משנה meant when it called the קרבן 'פסול' after the blood was put in the wrong spot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone could think 'פסול' means the whole קרבן failed. שמואל splits it into two results. The meat is forbidden to eat, but the owners' כפרה has already been accomplished.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that follows the משנה
The owners who brought the קרבן
They have been atoned for (received כפרה)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the whole סוגיא: the result for the meat and the result for the owners are different.

phrases.english: GEMARA
Shmuel says:
"Disqualified" refers to the meat,
but the owners have been atoned for.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: פָּסוּל בָּשָׂר, אֲבָל בְּעָלִים נִתְכַּפְּרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the ruling of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When blood is put on the wrong part of the מזבח, the meat is forbidden but the owners have received כפרה.

steps.title: The Source: Blood Reaching the Altar Atones
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives שמואל's reason. The פסוק says blood was given 'on the מזבח to atone', so once blood reaches the מזבח at all, the owners are atoned.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? The verse says: 'And I have given it to you upon the altar to atone.' This teaches that once the blood reaches the altar, the owners are atoned for.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why שמואל says the owners are atoned, and answers with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק simply says 'on the מזבח' without naming a specific spot. So שמואל learns that any contact of the blood with the מזבח brings כפרה, even if it was the wrong part.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
Because the verse says:
"And I have given it to you
upon the altar to atone" —
once the blood has reached the altar,
the owners are atoned for.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for שמואל's ruling
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's claim that the owners are atoned
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 17:11, 'ואני נתתיו לכם על המזבח לכפר'

steps.title: Then the Meat Should Be Permitted Too
steps.stepSummary: If blood anywhere on the מזבח works, the meat should also become permitted to eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the meat should be permitted as well!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges שמואל: if the blood 'worked', why only partly?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse was used to show the blood counts. A blood service that counts normally also permits the meat. So why does שמואל say the meat stays forbidden?

phrases.english: If so, the meat too should be permitted!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the split result of step 1 using the source from step 2
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that the meat is פסול
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the blood counts as a valid placement for כפרה, it should also permit the meat.

steps.title: 'To Atone': Only for Atonement
steps.stepSummary: The word 'לכפר' limits the rule. Blood in the wrong place gives כפרה, but it does nothing else, such as permitting the meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says 'to atone': I gave it for atonement, and not for anything else.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the פסוק itself limits what this blood accomplishes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'לכפר' is read as a limit. This kind of placement brings כפרה and nothing more. Permitting the meat is a separate result that does not come from this פסוק.

phrases.english: The verse says: "to atone" —
I gave it for atonement,
and not for anything else.
phrases.notes: Here the 'something else' is permitting the meat to be eaten.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: Blood that counts should permit the meat as well.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word 'לכפר' limits it: the blood brings כפרה only, and the meat stays forbidden.
steps.whatToRemember: According to שמואל, blood on the wrong part of the מזבח gives the owners כפרה, but the meat may not be eaten.

steps.title: שמואל Holds 'Wrong Place Counts as Right Place'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers that שמואל holds שלא במקומו כמקומו דמי: blood put in the wrong spot is treated as if it were in the right spot.
steps.simpleTranslation: So apparently he holds: blood placed not in its proper place is considered as if it were placed in its proper place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a general principle out of שמואל's ruling. This is a setup: the next step will challenge this principle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since שמואל says blood in the wrong spot still brings כפרה, he must view it as basically a proper placement. Putting it in these words lets the גמרא test it against another משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Blood in the wrong place counts as if it were in the right place

phrases.english: Apparently he holds:
blood not in its proper place is like blood in its proper place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a general principle out of שמואל's ruling, to prepare a challenge
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמואל holds שלא במקומו כמקומו דמי.

steps.title: A משנה: Wrong Placement Requires Redoing the Service
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה from another פרק. When blood is placed in various wrong spots, a fit כהן must collect fresh blood and do it again.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in another chapter: If he placed it on the ramp, or on a part of the altar not opposite the base; or placed blood meant for below the line above it, or blood meant for above below it; or blood meant for inside outside, or blood meant for outside inside — if the animal still has blood of the soul, the fit one should collect again.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source that seems to go against the principle from step 5. It is setting up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists cases of blood placed in the wrong spot. It rules that the service must be redone with new blood. That suggests the first placement did not count.

keyTerms.meaning: The ramp leading up to the מזבח
Life-blood still flowing from the animal
A כהן who is fit to serve

steps.confusionAlert: 'יחזור הכשר ויקבל' does not mean the old blood is collected again. A fit כהן collects new blood from the animal and does the service again.

phrases.english: We learned in another chapter:
If he placed it on the ramp
or on a spot not opposite the base;
phrases.notes: Some blood has to go on a part of the מזבח that stands above the base; this spot doesn't.

phrases.english: if he placed blood meant to go below, above;
phrases.notes: Below or above the red line that ran around the middle of the מזבח.

phrases.english: or blood meant to go above, below;
or blood meant to go inside, outside;
or blood meant to go outside, inside —
if there is still life-blood,
the fit one should collect again.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to test the principle from step 5
steps.kashyaTarget: The principle שלא במקומו כמקומו דמי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה requires redoing the service, so the wrong placement seems not to count.

steps.title: Why Redo It If the First Placement Counted?
steps.stepSummary: If the wrong placement counted as proper, there would be no reason for a fit כהן to collect new blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you think that blood not in its place is like blood in its place, why do I need the fit one to collect again?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states the challenge outright. The משנה's requirement to redo the service doesn't fit with שמואל's principle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the first placement had worked, it would already have done its job. Doing the service again only makes sense if the first one did not count.

phrases.english: And if it enters your mind
that not in its place is like in its place,
why do I need the fit one to collect again?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ שֶׁלֹּא בִּמְקוֹמוֹ כִּמְקוֹמוֹ, לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the challenge from the משנה quoted in step 6
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's view that blood in the wrong place counts
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Redoing the service would be pointless if the first placement had counted.

steps.title: The Redo Can't Be Just to Permit the Meat
steps.stepSummary: Someone might answer that the second service only permits the meat. The גמרא rejects this: no זריקה permits meat without also bringing כפרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say it's to permit the meat for eating — is there such a thing as a sprinkling that does not atone and yet permits the meat for eating?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא blocks a possible defense of שמואל. This leaves the challenge standing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The suggested answer splits the two results: the first placement gave כפרה, and the second only permits the meat. The גמרא says these cannot be split this way. Permitting the meat always comes with כפרה, so the second service must be needed for כפרה too.

keyTerms.meaning: Sprinkling or throwing the blood on the מזבח

phrases.english: And if you say
it is to permit the meat for eating —
is there a sprinkling that does not atone,
and yet permits the meat for eating?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects a possible answer to the challenge of step 7
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that the second service only permits the meat
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: No זריקה permits the meat without also bringing כפרה.
steps.whatToRemember: The challenge stands for now: the משנה requiring a redo implies that blood in the wrong place does not bring כפרה, which goes against שמואל.

steps.title: The משנה is talking about an unfit person placing the blood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees that if a fit כהן placed the blood in the wrong spot, it would count and no redo would be needed. It explains that the משנה is dealing with an unfit person who placed the blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a fit כהן had placed it, that is true: it would count. But here we are dealing with a case where an unfit person placed it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 7. The משנה that requires a fresh service is talking about blood that an unfit person placed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was: if the wrong spot counts as the right spot, why must a fit כהן collect new blood? The answer is that the first placement was done by a פסול, so it never counted at all. That is why a fit כהן must start again. The rule of שלא במקומו כמקומו דמי still stands for a fit כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: Fit, here meaning a כהן who is allowed to do the service
Unfit, here meaning a person who is not allowed to do the service
Here, what case are we dealing with? (introduces a narrower case)

phrases.english: If a fit one had placed it, so it is indeed;
phrases.notes: He means that a fit כהן's placement in the wrong spot really would count, and no redo would be needed.

phrases.english: here, with what are we dealing?
where an unfit person placed it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 7 after step 8 rejected the 'only to permit meat' answer
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to show that a wrong-spot placement by anyone does not count
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about a פסול placing the blood. A fit כהן's wrong-spot placement still counts.

steps.title: Then the offering should be permanently rejected
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: if an unfit person placed the blood, the offering should become דחוי and could not be fixed by a fit כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then let it be rejected for good!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer in step 9. It is about to bring a source to back up its challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The claim is that when a פסול does the זריקה, the offering is pushed off permanently (דחוי). If that is true, the משנה could not say a fit כהן collects new blood and fixes it. So the case in step 9 seems not to work.

keyTerms.meaning: Rejected; once pushed off, the offering cannot be fixed again

phrases.english: But let it be rejected!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the case suggested in step 9
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the משנה is about an unfit person placing the blood
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A זריקה by a פסול should make the offering דחוי, so a fit כהן could not redo it

steps.title: A משנה shows that sprinkling by the unfit cannot be redone
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה: if unfit people collected the blood with bad intent and more blood remains, a fit כהן may collect again. It infers that this works only after collecting, not after sprinkling, and suggests the reason is דחוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: all of them who collected the blood with intent for beyond its time or outside its place, if there is still blood of the soul, the fit one goes back and collects. Only if they collected, yes. If they sprinkled, no. What is the reason? Is it not because it becomes rejected?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to prove its challenge from step 10. It reads the משנה closely: it allows a redo only after collecting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה speaks only about unfit people collecting the blood. From this the גמרא infers that if they had sprinkled it, a fit כהן could not redo it. The natural reason seems to be that a זריקה by a פסול makes the offering דחוי.

keyTerms.meaning: Beyond its time: intent to eat or offer it after the allowed time
Outside its place: intent to eat or offer it outside the allowed area
Blood of the soul: the main blood that flows at שחיטה

phrases.english: As we learned:
And all of them who collected
phrases.notes: "All of them" means the unfit people listed earlier in that משנה.

phrases.english: beyond its time or outside its place,
if there is blood of the soul,
phrases.notes: He means the main blood is still flowing from the animal, so there is fresh blood to collect.

phrases.english: the fit one should go back and collect.
If they collected, yes; if they sprinkled, no;
What is the reason?
Is it not because it becomes rejected?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source behind the challenge of step 10
steps.raayaObject: That a זריקה by a פסול makes the offering דחוי
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about unfit people collecting with intent for חוץ לזמנו or חוץ למקומו, read closely: collecting, yes; sprinkling, no

steps.title: The reason is the bad intent, not דחוי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back on the proof: sprinkling cannot be redone because the bad intent disqualifies the offering, not because of דחוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It is because it is disqualified by the intent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the reasoning of step 11. It gives a different reason why a sprinkling by the unfit cannot be redone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case in that משנה had intent for beyond its time or outside its place. Such intent at the זריקה ruins the offering by itself. So the משנה does not prove that a פסול's זריקה makes it דחוי.

keyTerms.meaning: Intent: an improper thought during the service that can disqualify an offering

phrases.english: No; because it is disqualified by the intent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference drawn in step 11
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the reason given for the משנה's distinction, not the משנה itself
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The 'no redo after sprinkling' rule can be explained by the bad intent rather than by דחוי

steps.title: Then intent during collecting should disqualify too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: if intent is the reason, then intent during קבלה should also ruin the offering. Yet the משנה lets a fit כהן collect again.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, collecting should also be ruined!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer of step 12 with a first problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bad intent ruins an offering whether it comes during קבלה or during זריקה. If intent were the reason, the משנה could not allow a redo after the unfit people collected with bad intent. Since it does allow it, intent cannot be what makes the difference.

keyTerms.meaning: Collecting the blood in a vessel, one of the four main blood services

phrases.english: If so, the collection too!
phrases.notes: He means that collecting with bad intent should also ruin the offering, so no redo should be allowed.

steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that bad intent explains why sprinkling cannot be redone
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Intent works the same way at collecting and at sprinkling, but the משנה lets collecting be redone

steps.title: An unfit person's intent does not count at all
steps.stepSummary: A second objection: according to רבא, intent only counts when it comes from someone fit for the service. So an unfit person's intent should not disqualify anything.
steps.simpleTranslation: And besides, does intent disqualify here? Didn't רבא say: intent only works when it comes from someone fit for the service, about something fit for the service, and in a place fit for the service!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second, stronger attack on step 12, using a rule of רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא sets three conditions before intent can disqualify: a fit person, a fit item and a fit place. In our case the person doing the service is a פסול, so his intent should mean nothing. That knocks out the 'intent' explanation and brings back the challenge of step 10. The next step answers it.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore; introduces a second objection
Is effective, has power to change the status

steps.whyThisMatters: רבא's three conditions are a key rule in the laws of מחשבה. Improper intent only has power when everything else about the service is proper.

phrases.english: And furthermore, does intent disqualify?!
But didn't רבא say:
Intent is not effective
except with one who is fit for the service,
and with an item that is fit for the service,
and in a place that is fit for the service!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, independent objection to the defense in step 12
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the unfit person's bad intent disqualifies the offering
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to רבא, intent from someone not fit for the service has no power, so it cannot be the reason

steps.title: The inference is about slaughtering, not sprinkling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes what we infer from the משנה. The case with no fix is not 'they sprinkled' but 'they slaughtered'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do not say the inference is 'if they sprinkled, it cannot be fixed.' Rather, say it is 'if they slaughtered, it cannot be fixed.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the objections from steps 13 and 14 by reading the משנה's hidden inference differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An unfit person may do שחיטה, so his bad intent during שחיטה really counts and ruins the offering. קבלה and זריקה need a fit כהן, so an unfit person's intent at those stages means nothing, just as רבא said. That explains why a fit כהן can simply collect again after a bad קבלה.

keyTerms.meaning: Don't say... rather say: the גמרא replaces one reading with another

steps.confusionAlert: The 'no' in each phrase does not mean 'they may not sprinkle' or 'they may not slaughter.' It means the mistake cannot be fixed by a fit כהן.

phrases.english: Do not say: "If they sprinkled, no"
phrases.notes: 'No' here means a fit כהן can't fix it by doing the step again.

phrases.english: Rather say: "If they slaughtered, no"

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא תֵּימָא: זָרְקוּ לָא, אֶלָּא אֵימָא: שָׁחֲטוּ לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objections of steps 13–14 by changing the inference drawn in step 11
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the inference from the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה implies that after an unfit person sprinkles, the mistake cannot be fixed
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה implies that after an unfit person slaughters with bad intent, it cannot be fixed, because his intent counts during שחיטה

steps.title: Isn't this already stated in the משנה?
steps.stepSummary: If the point is that an unfit person's intent disqualifies during שחיטה, the משנה already says so openly.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is it teaching us, that intent disqualifies? We already learned: 'Therefore, they disqualify with intent!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new reading: if it only teaches that intent during שחיטה disqualifies, that is already written in a משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A משנה is not supposed to teach the same thing twice. The משנה says unfit people's שחיטה is valid, 'therefore they disqualify with intent.' So the inference from step 15 seems to add nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it teaching us? (asks what new point is being made)

phrases.english: What is it teaching us?
That intent disqualifies?
We already learned: "Therefore,
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה saying unfit people's slaughter is valid.

phrases.english: they disqualify with intent!"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 15 as repeating an explicit משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: The re-reading in step 15 (the inference is about שחיטה)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Redundancy: the משנה already says unfit people's intent disqualifies during slaughter

steps.title: The new point: from collection onward, their intent doesn't count
steps.stepSummary: The משנה's real point is that from קבלה onward an unfit person's intent does not disqualify, following רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it teaches us: from collection onward, intent does not disqualify. What is the reason? Like רבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה teaches something new: the limit. An unfit person's intent counts only at שחיטה, not from קבלה onward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The other משנה only says unfit people's intent works at שחיטה. This משנה adds that it stops working at קבלה and later steps. The reason is רבא's rule that intent only counts from someone fit for that particular service.

keyTerms.meaning: From the collection of the blood onward
Like רבא (his rule that intent counts only from one fit for the service)

steps.whatToRemember: An unfit person's bad intent ruins an offering only during שחיטה, which he is allowed to do. From קבלה onward his intent means nothing, following רבא.

phrases.english: This is what it teaches us:
that from collection onward
intent does not disqualify.
What is the reason? Like Rava.
phrases.notes: This is the rule of רבא from step 14.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the redundancy challenge of step 16
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifying a new point the משנה teaches
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The inference only repeats that unfit people disqualify with intent
steps.terutzMaskana: It teaches the limit: from קבלה onward an unfit person's intent does not disqualify, following רבא

steps.title: An objection from a ברייתא about blood placed in the wrong spot
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins quoting a ברייתא. Intending to place blood above or below the red line, to be done that same day, leaves the offering fit. The ברייתא then starts a case where he had intent again.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: if he intended to place the blood meant for above, below, or the blood meant for below, above, and to do it immediately, it is fit. (The standard printing also has: tomorrow, it is unfit; some versions leave this out.) If he then again had intent...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new objection from a ברייתא. Here it quotes only the opening; the actual challenge comes in the next part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some blood goes on the upper part of the מזבח and some on the lower part, divided by a red line. Intending to put it in the wrong part, to be done that same day, does not ruin the offering. The ברייתא now begins a case where he 'again had intent' at a later step. It deals with blood meant for the wrong part of the מזבח, the same subject as שמואל's principle. The rest of the ברייתא, and the challenge drawn from it, comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: Above / below the red line on the מזבח

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
If he intended to place those that are placed
above, below;
phrases.notes: Above or below the red line around the middle of the מזבח.

phrases.english: below, above;
immediately, it is fit.
(tomorrow, it is unfit.)
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out these words in round brackets.

phrases.english: He then again had intent

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new challenge from a ברייתא that returns to blood placed in the wrong spot, apparently against שמואל's principle in step 5. The quote and the challenge continue on the next amud.
steps.kashyaTarget: Most likely שמואל's principle שלא במקומו כמקומו דמי from step 5, since the ברייתא deals with blood meant for the wrong part of the מזבח. The ברייתא is still being quoted, and the challenge itself comes on the next amud.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Not yet stated; the ברייתא and the challenge continue on the next amud
